name: BashToolGuard
description: Blocks cat/head/tail file reading — enforces COMP-7 mechanically (Tier 3)

name: TopLevelCdGuard
description: Refuses a Bash command whose TOP LEVEL begins with or chains to `cd` — a top-level cd moves the SESSION's working directory, which worktree isolation resolves against, so it kills a peer agent's worktree creation hours later with no error naming the cause. Hard refusal, Jason's decision on #992, taken with the measured 32.7%-of-31,577 hit rate in hand; #1040 built the warn/block/off ladder and this takes `block` as the default, so RUNGATE_CD_GUARD=warn|off reverses it without a code change. Scoped to harnessed projects via lib/harness-project.ts. USER scope since #1578, correcting #992: it was `project` on the premise that ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is the worktree and every worktree carries the committed .claude/settings.json. The worktree does carry it and the session does not load it — measured in a worktree registering this hook, three bare `cd` calls went unrefused while user-scoped COMP-7 fired on the same Bash matcher in the same session, so the guard had been green, registered and inert since #1050. What it protects decides the scope: the SESSION's primary directory is machine-wide state and SC-518 governs it. The repo therefore reports it UNMEASURED and must NOT also register it in .claude/settings.json (SC-518: dual registration fires twice). Registered live in ~/.claude/settings.json (measured 2026-11-11, #1986); the session-start hook-currency reading reports it if this entry and the machine's registration ever disagree. The parse is lib/top-level-cd.ts; read its WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER block.

name: BunTestPathGuard
description: Refuses a Bash command that hands `bun test` a path matching no file. Bun treats an unmatched path argument as a name FILTER and exits non-zero only when NOTHING matched, so `bun test <real> <absent>` exits 0 and prints a pass total — measured on bun 1.3.14, #1544. A typo'd path in a verification command is therefore byte-identical to a suite that ran and passed, which is the sixth shape in .claude/rules/checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md inside the instrument every agent verifies its own work with. Bound to the Bash tool rather than a wrapper because 49 of this tree's 55 `bun test` exec sites are inside test/ and the failure that produced the issue was a command an agent composed by hand; a spawn from inside a running process is the declared gap. Warn/block/off ladder via RUNGATE_BUN_TEST_PATH_GUARD, default block. Scoped to harnessed projects via lib/harness-project.ts. The decision is lib/bun-test-paths.ts; read its WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER block.

name: TestSuiteGuard
description: Blocks a full test suite (bun test) once the worker has spent its rate — enforces DIR-L29 mechanically (Tier 3). The rate lives in lib/test-suite-lock.ts.

name: TestSuiteRelease
description: Hands a full suite its concurrency slot back when it finishes, so the next session is not stuck waiting out the 420s TTL (#67). Registered in user settings; #910 reported it registered nowhere after counting this file alone.

name: AgentBriefGuard
description: Validates agent brief templates and enforces ship-active marker

name: AgentVerdictCapture

name: AutoVerifyGate

name: CommitEnforcement

name: GateEnforcement

name: IssueCloseGuard
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, not harness-only. Couples to two things a fresh consumer does not have: a GitHub issue tracker wired to ship-gate, and the HMAC `.gate-salt` it validates PASS provenance against. With neither present it declines on every call, and a guard that declines on every call is indistinguishable from one that is not installed. It ships in the tarball; a project registers it once ship-gate runs against its tracker.
description: Blocks gh issue close without ship-gate PASS and HMAC validation

name: MergeGuard
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, not harness-only. Reads `.ship-active` markers under WORK_DIR and a verify-gate PASS out of workflow-state.json; a project that has not run the ship loop has neither, so it warns about nothing. Ships in the tarball; register it once the ship loop runs.
description: Early warning on git merge to main without verify-gate passing

name: PostCompact
description: Re-injects critical rules after context window compaction

name: SpecConformityTrigger
notDeployedReason: HARNESS-ONLY, and downstream of `enabled: false` — see disabledReason. A disabled entry that also claimed consumer deployment would be two answers to one question. Re-classify if and when it is re-enabled.
description: Auto-runs conformity when spec files are modified
disabledReason: package.json already runs scripts/sync-sc-status.ts as posttest, so this would be a second decider for one question — the fourth shape in .claude/rules/checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md, where a mutation of either leaves the other holding the case up. The two triggers are also not equivalent, and the posttest one is the better of them: it ticks coverage after a suite run, where this one ticks it on a text edit, with no test having been run. #479.

name: SpecSCGuard
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, not harness-only. Validates new SC lines against `config/matcher-registry.json`, which means it has nothing to say until the project has specs carrying SCs. Ships in the tarball; register it once `specs/` exists.
description: Validates new SC lines in spec files have matching patterns

name: HookCurrency
description: Reports installed git hooks that are not the generator output (#879), and how many commits behind main the tree each Claude Code hook registration resolves to is (#1216)

name: StaleTTLCleanup
notDeployedReason: HARNESS-ONLY. It is not the `cleanStaleFiles` sweep its header advertises: sixty lines down, behind `await import('../lib/branch-cleanup.ts')`, it calls `cleanupStaleBranches({maxAgeDays: 7})`, which walks `refs/remotes/origin/*` and runs `git push origin --delete <branch>` on each one it judges stale. The two preconditions this entry named are now BOTH met by #1079, and neither alone would have been enough. (1) The slug: `hasOpenPR` used to default to `hornjason/pai-harness` when no `repo` was passed — which the hook does not pass — so on a consumer the open-PR question was asked about THIS repository, their branch names were absent from it, `hasPR` came back false with no error, and the delete ran against THEIR origin. It failed OPEN precisely for the equipped consumer, because this repository is PUBLIC and any valid token reads our PRs successfully and returns the empty list that authorises the deletion. `resolveRepoSlug` now reads the slug from the calling project's own `origin` remote and an unresolvable one is UNMEASURED, which REFUSES the delete and says so; there is no fallback literal left in the module. (2) The arming: the branch-deletion arm is disarmed unless `RUNGATE_BRANCH_CLEANUP=1`, read through the one exported `branchCleanupArmedFromEnv` binding, the way `reapOrphans` is armed through `armedFromEnv`. STILL NOT DEPLOYED, and the reason is now a different one: the worktree, scratch-dir and orphan-reaper arms of this same hook have never been separately cleared for consumer use and need their own reading. Deploying it is blocked on that, not on the branch arm.
description: Cleans up stale workflow-state.json and ship-active files

name: TaskCompleted
notDeployedReason: HARNESS-ONLY, and downstream of `enabled: false` — see disabledReason. It spawns a CONCURRENT full suite, which is the thing lib/test-suite-lock.ts exists to prevent, so deploying it to a consumer would export the defect that disabled it here. Re-classify if and when it is re-enabled.
description: Quality gates before task completion (tests, uncommitted changes, conformity)
disabledReason: checkTests spawns a full bun test with a 120000 ms timeout and this suite measures around 400 s, so the run can never finish — every completion would report a timed-out non-zero exit with no parseable failure count, which the code turns into a warning. It also spawns a CONCURRENT full suite, which is what DIR-L29 and lib/test-suite-lock.ts exist to prevent and what jetsam-killed the machine once already. Re-enable only after the timeout exceeds the measured suite duration and the spawn goes through the suite lock. #479.

name: VerifyPhaseLock
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, not harness-only. Blocks `gh issue create` during the VERIFY phase, so it presumes both a GitHub tracker and an active rungate workflow. Ships in the tarball; register it once the project ships through phases against a tracker.
description: Gates gh issue create: the VERIFY-phase lock, and the finding adjudication (#1261)

name: WorkflowStateGuard
description: Blocks direct Write/Edit of workflow-state.json

name: ProjectStateSync
notDeployedReason: HARNESS-ONLY today, by two independent facts and not by preference. It execs `<projectRoot>/scripts/update-project-state.ts`, which `package.json` `files[]` does not publish, so on a consumer `projectStateTarget` returns `declined-no-generator` on every write — zero reading as success, the shape #1047 is about. And #910's #296 blast-radius question is open: it is registered on BOTH Write and Edit at user scope, so it would fire on every agent edit in a consumer's worktree, and PROJECT-STATE.md is DA-owned. Deploying it is blocked on publishing the generator AND closing #910; revisit on either, not on neither.
description: Regenerates PROJECT-STATE.md when project-state.json is written. Registered in user settings on BOTH Write and Edit; whether it should fire on every agent edit is open on #910 (#296 blast radius).

name: ActionVerificationGate
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, and the strongest candidate of #713's seven. Zero file I/O, zero PAI paths, one import — it regex-matches state-changing Bash and injects a verify-before-reporting reminder, which behaves identically on a repo that has never heard of rungate. It is false here only because #713 moves files into the package and does not decide deployment; #1084 is why those are separate commits. Recommend true in the follow-up that turns deployment on.
description: Injects a verify-before-reporting reminder after a state-changing Bash command appears to succeed. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.

name: BashWriteGuard
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, with one blast-radius question to settle before it travels. Every artifact it protects (workflow-state.json, .gate-salt, witnesses/) is a rungate gate artifact, so a consumer running gates wants it. But it also blocks ALL Bash writes to any *.hook.ts, and a consumer AUTHORING hooks would hit that guard on their own files with a message about gate integrity. Decide whether the hook-file arm should be scoped to the rungate hooks directory before setting true.
description: Blocks Bash writes to gate artifacts and hook files, and chmod/chflags on hook files. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.

name: DocHygiene
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN. The shippability blocker is gone: #1119 removed the `owner: jason` literal, and the key is now omitted rather than defaulted, so a consumer's markdown carries nothing this repository chose for them. What remains is a taste decision, not a defect — stamping a doc header on every markdown a consumer writes is a convention they should opt into, and nothing here can tell whether they want it. Flip this to true only alongside a way for a consumer to decline it. Migrated under #713.
description: Stamps the four required frontmatter fields onto markdown docs and reports docs missing from DOCS.md. Thin trigger over lib/frontmatter.ts. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.

name: GateResultProtection
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN. Pure rungate gate integrity — it refuses a Write or Edit that sets gates.*.result or phase DONE in workflow-state.json directly instead of through the gate runner, and it reads no path outside the file the tool call already names. A consumer running gates needs exactly this, so it should travel once #713's follow-up turns deployment on. False here only because this PR adds files to the package and does not enable deployment.
description: Blocks direct Write/Edit of gate result fields and phase DONE in workflow-state.json. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.

name: HarnessAFKGate
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, and self-limiting: it blocks AskUserQuestion only while the most recent PRD under WORK_DIR sits in build/execute/verify, and allows everything when no PRD exists at all, so on a consumer who never runs an AFK harness it is inert. The PRD-driven ship lifecycle is rungate's own, so it belongs with the product. Gate it on the consumer actually using AFK runs rather than on scaffold time.
description: Blocks AskUserQuestion while a PRD is in a post-approval phase, so AFK runs are not stalled on a prompt. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.

name: SkillGuard
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN, and the case for deploying it is the strongest of the seven on the merits: the keybindings-help position-bias false positive is a Claude Code platform defect that reaches every consumer equally, and BLOCKED_SKILLS plus one import is the entire hook. The argument against is that it hard-codes an opinion about a FIRST-PARTY skill, so a consumer gets a block they never configured. Worth Jason's call rather than an agent's.
description: Blocks the keybindings-help position-bias false positive. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.

name: TeamInit
notDeployedReason: OPT-IN. It writes teams/session-<id>/config.json under Claude Code's OWN configuration directory, which exists on every machine running Claude Code whether or not PAI is installed, and the compaction bug it fixes hits any agent-spawning product. It is idempotent and exits zero on every error path. False here only because #713 does not enable deployment; it also writes outside the consumer's repo, which is worth stating out loud before it travels.
description: Creates the per-session team config whose absence makes typed agent spawns fail after compaction. Migrated from ~/.pai/hooks by #713.
